Delegate breakdown by county. Obtained by Drop Site News and
The tension between organizers and Maine Democratic party officials has grown as they determine a process to replace Platner. A former Platner staffer told Drop Site "all field and data" staff were moved onto MDP payroll before the rape allegations broke for "accounting purposes," creating an awkward situation for the Platner organizers--who, like the volunteers, are unhappy with the MDP's manuevers.
On July 8, Platner campaign organizing director Spencer Toth resigned from the MDP over its lack of engagement with volunteers and organizers in determining the replacement process. [Drop Site obtained his resignation letter.](https://substack.com/redirect/e0ff7d58-e584-4d55-a96e-ede5fe57ecf5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
"Together, organizers and volunteers built something much bigger than one candidate. They built the largest grassroots operation in Maine's history, a people powered movement rooted in working class politics and the belief that ordinary Mainers deserve a real voice in the future of the Democratic party," Toth's resignation letter says. "But yesterday, the Maine Democratic Party said the people who built this movement will "have no role in determining our next Democratic nominee for US Senate, nor in determining what this process looks like."
[The MDP Executive Director Devon Murphy-Anderson](https://substack.com/redirect/16c46c33-7df9-415d-8a57-f6ba48548f5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) had accused the Platner team of "trying to tip the scales" by asking for transparency on the replacement process. "We have repeatedly reiterated to Graham Platner's team that they have no role in determining our next Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate, nor in determining what this process looks like."
"That work matters. It cannot be treated as disposable. The people who knocked thousands of doors, organized their communities, and built local teams across the state deserve transparency, respect, and a meaningful voice in what comes next."
Toth concludes there is "no path forward to defeating Susan Collins without honoring and engaging the grassroots movement" the Platner campaign built across Maine. The future of the race should not be decided without the people who made the movement possible, Toth says.
"You deserve to have your voice heard and it is incumbent on each of you now to hold the Democratic Party accountable."
Volunteers for Platner have [broadly supported](https://substack.com/redirect/8c50e2c3-02d5-4494-a5cd-49e1e34692bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the nomination of Troy Jackson in place of Platner. On Friday morning, the Maine AFL-CIO also endorsed Jackson.
"We can pass Medicare for all, we can take on corporate power and the politicians in their pocket," Jackson said in his Senate [announcement video](https://substack.com/redirect/7ad4c7a6-b052-4e2a-b8e2-b80cb82232e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). "I've won in deep red Trump country and progressive cities like Portland and Bangor. His full senate policy platform is yet to be released.

body:

Hello Peter,
Earlier this year, veteran members of our community protested against Brad Knott after his refusal to hold an in-person town hall and his office's failure to respond to repeated calls about ongoing firings at the VA. Our veterans fought for our right to freedom and deserve respect, not a telephone town hall that you have to pre-register for.
My opponent has accepted over $200k from a combination of PACs that have continued to advocate against the best interests of our community, including health insurance, agribusiness, and energy PACs, as well as $10k from sugar industry interests that benefit from the current administration's tariffs, which are raising food prices.
Over the last few weeks of June, our campaign held a town hall in every county in the district, and those conversations were some of the most enlightening I have had so far. We also reached out to Knott’s office to invite him and never heard back.
My campaign has been built on grassroots support and almost entirely from individual donors; I have not accepted any money from corporate PACs because that’s not who I am here to represent. My neighbors, like you, are supporting me because we know that working together is how we’re finally going to start fixing our government.
So here’s the bottom line: I’m meeting with the people in District 13 multiple times a week, every week. I live here, and this is my home, and I am running for this seat because Washington does not work for us anymore, and that has to change. My opponent seems to only have time for curated audiences, lobbyists, and a photo op. We deserve better representation than this.
I am relying on grassroots support from voters like you, who know how important a change in leadership is for our community. Can you chip in any amount today to keep propelling our campaign forward? Every donation gets us one step closer to sending Brad Knott back home in November. [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/barringeremails?refcode=20260710]

* **Health care costs skyrocketed.** More than 17,000 people across Dutchess, Orange, and Ulster Counties have already been kicked off their health insurance. Families across the region are staring down massive ACA premium hikes, with some facing increases of up to $1,000 a month.
* **Local farmers and food banks got hit hard.** Trump’s USDA cuts have pulled support away from Hudson Valley farms and food banks, with millions fewer meals expected to reach families in need.
* **Food assistance was put at risk.** Up to 74,000 people in the Hudson Valley were put at risk of losing some or all of their SNAP benefits, leaving working families, seniors, veterans, and children to pay the price.

Ro Khanna wants voters to see the new version of Ro Khanna: anti-oligarch, anti-stock-trading, anti-billionaire, anti-establishment, and suddenly fluent in the language of economic populism.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ae1e3d9e-5a1b-4be6-b774-c90a24635689?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Congressman Rohit Khanna
That is the version Ro Khanna is selling now. I do not buy it. This does not look like conviction. It looks like a wealthy Silicon Valley politician trying on working-class rage because he figured out that is the uniform for 2028.
Khanna did not come out of nowhere as some working-class revolt against Silicon Valley power. He came up as a Silicon Valley Democrat, backed by the tech world, representing one of the richest and most powerful districts in America. [Business Insider described his 2016 victory as a win for the tech industry ](https://substack.com/redirect/94dd07b9-0571-4ec8-8530-eeb937fcb6d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)and said he had been a favorite of the tech industry since his 2014 run against Mike Honda.
Now he wants to sound like the man who will save the Democratic Party from billionaires. That is the part Democrats should examine before they start treating him like the answer for 2028 and before we welcome him into our state and congressional races.
* * *
## Who Is Ro Khanna
Ro Khanna, full name Rohit Khanna, was born on September 13, 1976, in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. He is 49 years old. His parents immigrated to the United States from Punjab, India, in 1968. His father was a chemical engineer, and his mother was a former schoolteacher. Khanna grew up in Bucks County, Pennsylvania, before going on to the University of Chicago, where he earned a degree in economics, and Yale Law School, where he earned his law degree.
Before Congress, Khanna worked as an attorney, taught at Stanford, Santa Clara University School of Law, and San Francisco State University, and served in the Obama administration as deputy assistant secretary at the U.S. Department of Commerce from 2009 to 2011. After leaving the Commerce Department, he joined Wilson Sonsini, a Silicon Valley law firm, and later worked as vice president of strategic initiatives at Smart Utility Systems.
Politically, Khanna first ran for Congress in 2004 and lost. He later challenged Democratic incumbent Mike Honda in California's 17th Congressional District in 2014 and lost again, though his campaign was heavily backed by major names in the tech industry. In 2016, he ran again, defeated Honda, and has represented California's 17th District since January 2017. The district includes a major part of Silicon Valley, which is central to understanding both his rise and the criticism of his current populist rebrand
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/05c0b94a-c80c-4088-b55e-6127f2d63d5f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Khanna Called Most Reliant on Funding from Wall Street 2016](https://substack.com/redirect/a8327ab2-d3e4-4e09-9fee-db6f7aa0698d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Khanna now describes himself as a "progressive capitalist." He endorsed Bernie Sanders in 2016, co-chaired Sanders' 2020 presidential campaign, sits in the Congressional Progressive Caucus, and has built a national profile around antitrust, technology, manufacturing, foreign policy restraint, campaign finance reform, and economic populism. He is married to Ritu Ahuja Khanna, and they have two children.

## Before the Populist Rebrand
Khanna's political origin was not anti-tech populism. He was Silicon Valley all day. The tech bros of bros!
He represented the tech district. He raised from the tech ecosystem. He built the profile of the polished, pro-innovation, Silicon Valley Democrat who could speak the language of startups, global competition, and the new economy.
But now the language has changed.
Now Khanna talks about economic patriotism, steel towns, manufacturing, workers left behind, and the failure of both parties to build an economy that reaches beyond the coasts. His own "[New Economic Patriotism](https://substack.com/redirect/25774092-a248-4faf-8fa8-c3628ca4fc00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" pitch opens with steelworkers in Chicago, shuttered mills, lower-paying warehouse jobs, and the decline of opportunity for working-class communities. He relaunched the whole vision in an [April 2026 National Press Club speech](https://substack.com/redirect/220616b6-5e31-4b91-9f2f-d20e98e781f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that pivots from "the Epstein class" of untouchable elites straight to "we need a billionaire tax."
That is a real issue. The problem is not that Ro Khanna is talking about it. The problem is that every version of Ro Khanna seems to arrive exactly when that version becomes useful. The grifter that knows the right time to change the grift and use people to shape his brand and perception.

## Ro Khanna Is Borrowing Other People's Working-Class Credibility
Khanna's endorsements are not random. They are a map. He is attaching himself to the exact kinds of candidates who signal where the Democratic base is moving: democratic socialists, labor candidates, anti-establishment candidates, and working-class messengers outside his Silicon Valley lane. ABC News reported that Khanna has backed more than 30 candidates this cycle, with national attention on his endorsement strategy as he is widely viewed as a possible 2028 contender.
The old Ro Khanna was the Silicon Valley Democrat. The new Ro Khanna wants to be seen standing next to socialists, union workers, and populists. So who is he endorsing?
* **Zohran Mamdani, New York City mayor**
Mamdani gives Khanna the DSA lane. NYC-DSA endorsed Mamdani, and his campaign became a national symbol of movement from the left before he won City Hall. For Khanna, standing with Mamdani is a way to look aligned with the socialist energy inside the Democratic base without having to actually be from that world.
* **Omar Fateh, Minneapolis mayoral candidate**
Fateh gives Khanna another democratic socialist signal, this time in Minneapolis. The Progressive described Fateh's rise as part of a "Mamdani Moment" in Minneapolis, with democratic socialist candidates making gains against Democratic establishment resistance. Fateh, a Minnesota state senator, won the DFL endorsement but lost the November 2025 race to incumbent Jacob Frey. Winning was never the point for Khanna. That is exactly the kind of fight Khanna wants to be photographed near now.
* **Brian Poindexter, Ohio 's 7th Congressional District**
Poindexter gives Khanna the labor lane. Poindexter is a union ironworker, organizer, Brook Park city councilman, and Democrat running against Max Miller in Ohio's 7th. Working Families Party endorsed him as a working-class candidate, and America's Work Force Union Podcast described him as an Ironworkers Local 17 member campaigning on wages, health care, and retirement security. Khanna endorsing him is not just about Ohio. It lets Khanna borrow the credibility from labor in a working-class district far from Silicon Valley.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ad0d539b-ece8-45f6-8bab-e456f684de33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Abdul El-Sayed, Michigan U.S. Senate**
El-Sayed gives Khanna the Bernie-left, anti-corporate Senate lane. El-Sayed is running on taxing billionaires, Medicare for All, and breaking up corporate power, and he oversaw an effort to erase hundreds of millions in medical debt as Wayne County's health director ([Time, July 8, 2026](https://substack.com/redirect/02c616cd-210c-4fdb-b1a9-575b55b4c947?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). That fits perfectly with Khanna's new anti-billionaire language. Maybe he is just jealous he isn't a billionaire yet. More on that later. Believe that.
* **Graham Platner, Maine U.S. Senate**
Platner gave Khanna the rural anti-establishment lane before the campaign blew up. ABC listed Platner among Khanna's Senate endorsements. After a serious sexual-assault allegation surfaced, Khanna rescinded his endorsement and publicly called on Platner to drop out ([Fox News, July 6, 2026](https://substack.com/redirect/67ee1a00-d1c2-43ab-901e-80f8e8df8ab7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). That does not erase the original political calculation: Platner was part of the tough guy working man image.

Turek gives Khanna a Midwestern Senate lane. He fits the broader pattern of Khanna trying to build relationships outside California in states that matter for Senate control and presidential politics. ABC listed Turek among Khanna's Senate endorsements.
* **Roy Cooper, North Carolina U.S. Senate**
Cooper gives Khanna a more establishment-friendly lane. This is important because Khanna cannot be seen as not only endorsing DSA and Labor. He is also covering himself with electability and swing-state credibility.

## His New Script

---|---|---
[https://www.foxbusiness.com/politics/progressive-lawmakers-bernie-sanders-ro-khanna-unveil-4-4t-wealth-tax-targeting-billionaires](https://substack.com/redirect/8bcf80b4-35be-4abd-ab88-f006457d1230?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Khanna is now teaming with Bernie Sanders on a billionaire wealth tax. Their bill, the Make Billionaires Pay Their Fair Share Act, would place a 5% annual tax on the roughly 938 billionaires in America and use the revenue for $3,000 direct payments to working- and middle-income households and other working-family priorities.
But then let's stop pretending the obvious question is off the table. If Ro Khanna believes concentrated wealth is such a moral and political emergency, why is his own family wealth structured like the exact thing he is supposedly running against?
[A Free Beacon review of his financial disclosures](https://substack.com/redirect/271f778a-5860-4962-90a6-f3c66d6cd8c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) estimated family assets ranging from **$103 million to more than $340 million** across Khanna, his wife, and his children. His children reportedly hold tens of millions of dollars in irrevocable trusts. His wife and children's trusts are tied to thousands of stock trades. His [children's trusts reportedly hold interests in private golf clubs in Ohio that generate millions of dollars.](https://substack.com/redirect/3e1c585a-4e5b-44ad-897f-c3ef91968651?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
So...umm... wtaf?
Wealth is a problem when billionaires have it, but when it is [Ro Khanna's family, it is just estate planning? Stock trading is a problem when members of Congress do it](https://substack.com/redirect/05b8496f-e465-45ce-a7b8-2b35351d7534?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but when the trades run through spouse and child trusts, suddenly we are all supposed to be ok with nearly $56 million in trades? Hoarded wealth is bad, but golf course interests tucked into children's trusts are just normal family business? Good?
Khanna is full of shit.
If Khanna believes this much wealth should be redirected toward working families, why is he waiting for Congress to force him into that position? Why not move first?
Why not put a serious chunk of that family wealth into housing, medical debt relief, labor organizing, local journalism, rural hospitals, or worker-owned businesses? Why not build the kind of public-serving foundation he says the ultra-rich should be forced to fund?
Instead, voters are looking at trusts, private investments, real estate, stock activity, and golf club interests.
That is not working-class politics. That is a rich-guy pandering.
The issue is not whether Ro Khanna has technically violated the law. The issue is that he wants to campaign as the guy fighting concentrated wealth while his own household looks like a fucking case study in how concentrated wealth protects itself.

## So How Much Does Ro Have?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/02cb632f-f217-4904-9b38-4a1d03ce9ed4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[https://sfstandard.com/2026/03/03/ro-khanna-ethan-agarwal-congress/](https://substack.com/redirect/0c8edf8b-4631-4708-831f-cdadd428b2d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Common Cause reported that members of Congress made 13,324 trades totaling $635.57 million over the trailing year. In that same report, Khanna was listed third by volume, with 3,923 trades and $55.7 million in volume.
Khanna's defense is also part of the record. He says he does not personally own or trade stocks. He says the household investments are in a trust his in-laws set up before marriage, managed independently by a third-party trustee. He says neither he nor his wife directs the trades. He also points out that he supports the TRUST in Congress Act, which would bar members of Congress, their spouses, and their dependent children from trading individual stocks while in office.
Here's the obvious question. If spouses and dependent children belong inside the ban, why are voters supposed to pretend spousal and child trusts are irrelevant right now?
That's the contradiction. Not that there's proven insider trading. There is no public evidence proving that. The contradiction is that Khanna wants credit for supporting a ban that recognizes the household as part of the ethical problem, while asking voters to treat his own household as some separate universe.
That IS the Democratic hypocrisy.

## Give Him the Credit He Earned
Khanna does have a real anti-PAC record.
He launched the NO PAC Caucus in 2017, aimed at limiting PAC influence and prohibiting PAC contributions to members of Congress. He also joined Summer Lee, Pramila Jayapal, Rashida Tlaib, and others on the Abolish Super PACs Act in 2025.
This is not an argument that Ro Khanna has never done anything right. This is an argument that Democrats should stop confusing a well-timed rebrand with conviction.

## Laura's Take
Ro Khanna is an opportunist. He takes whichever position is selling that year and leaves his money exactly where it is.
In 2016 he ran as Silicon Valley's candidate, funded by the tech industry that had backed him since his first run at Mike Honda in 2014. In 2026 he is co-writing a billionaire wealth tax with Bernie Sanders. He is still the third-heaviest stock trader in Congress, $55.7 million across nearly 4,000 trades, while carrying his own bill to ban members of Congress from trading stocks. I believe Khanna does things like this because he knows the value of performative politics and understands it will never pass. Again, he is buying good will without doing any actual work. Ro Khanna is no better than Donald Trump in this category. Trump continues to use public office to grow his own fortune, and Khanna, no doubt, relies on insider-trading of some sort to do the same.
He has no working-class record, so he buys proximity to one. He endorsed Brian Poindexter, an ironworker in Ohio, Zohran Mamdani, a democratic socialist in New York, and Senate candidates in Maine, Michigan, Iowa, and North Carolina, none of them his home state. Not one of those endorsements changed a line in his own financial disclosures. They changed his photographs and his personal brand marketing.
Khanna represents Silicon Valley, by many measures the wealthiest congressional district in the country. The ironworkers, steel towns, and warehouse workers he now stands beside are not his constituents, but they now serve as his backdrop. The real Ro Khanna is "wet-fingered" (see the show Veep and its definition of the politics of Qataris) and if it became trendy to jump off bridges tomorrow, he'd be the first one to go. Who is Ro Khanna? Nobody as any actual idea.

He has no working-class record, so he endorses one -- an ironworker here, a socialist there, while he continues to be one of the top stock traders in congress. | | , , and | Jul 10 | | | | | ---|---|---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | Ro Khanna wants voters to see the new version of Ro Khanna: anti-oligarch, anti-stock-trading, anti-billionaire, anti-establishment, and suddenly fluent in the language of economic populism. | | ---|---|--- Congressman Rohit Khanna That is the version Ro Khanna is selling now. I do not buy it. This does not look like conviction. It looks like a wealthy Silicon Valley politician trying on working-class rage because he figured out that is the uniform for 2028. Khanna did not come out of nowhere as some working-class revolt against Silicon Valley power. He came up as a Silicon Valley Democrat, backed by the tech world, representing one of the richest and most powerful districts in America. said he had been a favorite of the tech industry since his 2014 run against Mike Honda. Now he wants to sound like the man who will save the Democratic Party from billionaires. That is the part Democrats should examine before they start treating him like the answer for 2028 and before we welcome him into our state and congressional races. Who Is Ro Khanna Ro Khanna, full name Rohit Khanna, was born on September 13, 1976, in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. He is 49 years old. His parents immigrated to the United States from Punjab, India, in 1968. His father was a chemical engineer, and his mother was a former schoolteacher. Khanna grew up in Bucks County, Pennsylvania, before going on to the University of Chicago, where he earned a degree in economics, and Yale Law School, where he earned his law degree. Before Congress, Khanna worked as an attorney, taught at Stanford, Santa Clara University School of Law, and San Francisco State University, and served in the Obama administration as deputy assistant secretary at the U.S. Department of Commerce from 2009 to 2011. After leaving the Commerce Department, he joined Wilson Sonsini, a Silicon Valley law firm, and later worked as vice president of strategic initiatives at Smart Utility Systems. Politically, Khanna first ran for Congress in 2004 and lost. He later challenged Democratic incumbent Mike Honda in California's 17th Congressional District in 2014 and lost again, though his campaign was heavily backed by major names in the tech industry. In 2016, he ran again, defeated Honda, and has represented California's 17th District since January 2017. The district includes a major part of Silicon Valley, which is central to understanding both his rise and the criticism of his current populist rebrand | | ---|---|--- Khanna now describes himself as a "progressive capitalist." He endorsed Bernie Sanders in 2016, co-chaired Sanders' 2020 presidential campaign, sits in the Congressional Progressive Caucus, and has built a national profile around antitrust, technology, manufacturing, foreign policy restraint, campaign finance reform, and economic populism. He is married to Ritu Ahuja Khanna, and they have two children. Before the Populist Rebrand Khanna's political origin was not anti-tech populism. He was Silicon Valley all day. The tech bros of bros! He represented the tech district. He raised from the tech ecosystem. He built the profile of the polished, pro-innovation, Silicon Valley Democrat who could speak the language of startups, global competition, and the new economy. But now the language has changed. Now Khanna talks about economic patriotism, steel towns, manufacturing, workers left behind, and the failure of both parties to build an economy that reaches beyond the coasts. His own "" pitch opens with steelworkers in Chicago, shuttered mills, lower-paying warehouse jobs, and the decline of opportunity for working-class communities. He relaunched the whole vision in an that pivots from "the Epstein class" of untouchable elites straight to "we need a billionaire tax." That is a real issue. The problem is not that Ro Khanna is talking about it. The problem is that every version of Ro Khanna seems to arrive exactly when that version becomes useful. The grifter that knows the right time to change the grift and use people to shape his brand and perception. Ro Khanna Is Borrowing Other People's Working-Class Credibility Khanna's endorsements are not random. They are a map. He is attaching himself to the exact kinds of candidates who signal where the Democratic base is moving: democratic socialists, labor candidates, anti-establishment candidates, and working-class messengers outside his Silicon Valley lane. ABC News reported that Khanna has backed more than 30 candidates this cycle, with national attention on his endorsement strategy as he is widely viewed as a possible 2028 contender. The old Ro Khanna was the Silicon Valley Democrat. The new Ro Khanna wants to be seen standing next to socialists, union workers, and populists. So who is he endorsing? Zohran Mamdani, New York City mayor Mamdani gives Khanna the DSA lane. NYC-DSA endorsed Mamdani, and his campaign became a national symbol of movement from the left before he won City Hall. For Khanna, standing with Mamdani is a way to look aligned with the socialist energy inside the Democratic base without having to actually be from that world. Omar Fateh, Minneapolis mayoral candidate Fateh gives Khanna another democratic socialist signal, this time in Minneapolis. The Progressive described Fateh's rise as part of a "Mamdani Moment" in Minneapolis, with democratic socialist candidates making gains against Democratic establishment resistance. Fateh, a Minnesota state senator, won the DFL endorsement but lost the November 2025 race to incumbent Jacob Frey. Winning was never the point for Khanna. That is exactly the kind of fight Khanna wants to be photographed near now. Brian Poindexter, Ohio 's 7th Congressional District Poindexter gives Khanna the labor lane. Poindexter is a union ironworker, organizer, Brook Park city councilman, and Democrat running against Max Miller in Ohio's 7th. Working Families Party endorsed him as a working-class candidate, and America's Work Force Union Podcast described him as an Ironworkers Local 17 member campaigning on wages, health care, and retirement security. Khanna endorsing him is not just about Ohio. It lets Khanna borrow the credibility from labor in a working-class district far from Silicon Valley. | | ---|---|--- Abdul El-Sayed, Michigan U.S. Senate El-Sayed gives Khanna the Bernie-left, anti-corporate Senate lane. El-Sayed is running on taxing billionaires, Medicare for All, and breaking up corporate power, and he oversaw an effort to erase hundreds of millions in medical debt as Wayne County's health director (). That fits perfectly with Khanna's new anti-billionaire language. Maybe he is just jealous he isn't a billionaire yet. More on that later. Believe that. Graham Platner, Maine U.S. Senate Platner gave Khanna the rural anti-establishment lane before the campaign blew up. ABC listed Platner among Khanna's Senate endorsements. After a serious sexual-assault allegation surfaced, Khanna rescinded his endorsement and publicly called on Platner to drop out (). That does not erase the original political calculation: Platner was part of the tough guy working man image. | | ---|---|--- Josh Turek, Iowa U.S. Senate Turek gives Khanna a Midwestern Senate lane. He fits the broader pattern of Khanna trying to build relationships outside California in states that matter for Senate control and presidential politics. ABC listed Turek among Khanna's Senate endorsements. Roy Cooper, North Carolina U.S. Senate Cooper gives Khanna a more establishment-friendly lane. This is important because Khanna cannot be seen as not only endorsing DSA and Labor. He is also covering himself with electability and swing-state credibility. His New Script | | ---|---|--- Khanna is now teaming with Bernie Sanders on a billionaire wealth tax. Their bill, the Make Billionaires Pay Their Fair Share Act, would place a 5% annual tax on the roughly 938 billionaires in America and use the revenue for $3,000 direct payments to working- and middle-income households and other working-family priorities. But then let's stop pretending the obvious question is off the table. If Ro Khanna believes concentrated wealth is such a moral and political emergency, why is his own family wealth structured like the exact thing he is supposedly running against? estimated family assets ranging from $103 million to more than $340 million across Khanna, his wife, and his children. His children reportedly hold tens of millions of dollars in irrevocable trusts. His wife and children's trusts are tied to thousands of stock trades. His So...umm... wtaf? Wealth is a problem when billionaires have it, but when it is , but when the trades run through spouse and child trusts, suddenly we are all supposed to be ok with nearly $56 million in trades? Hoarded wealth is bad, but golf course interests tucked into children's trusts are just normal family business? Good? Khanna is full of shit. If Khanna believes this much wealth should be redirected toward working families, why is he waiting for Congress to force him into that position? Why not move first? Why not put a serious chunk of that family wealth into housing, medical debt relief, labor organizing, local journalism, rural hospitals, or worker-owned businesses? Why not build the kind of public-serving foundation he says the ultra-rich should be forced to fund? Instead, voters are looking at trusts, private investments, real estate, stock activity, and golf club interests. That is not working-class politics. That is a rich-guy pandering. The issue is not whether Ro Khanna has technically violated the law. The issue is that he wants to campaign as the guy fighting concentrated wealth while his own household looks like a fucking case study in how concentrated wealth protects itself. So How Much Does Ro Have? | | ---|---|--- Common Cause reported that members of Congress made 13,324 trades totaling $635.57 million over the trailing year. In that same report, Khanna was listed third by volume, with 3,923 trades and $55.7 million in volume. Khanna's defense is also part of the record. He says he does not personally own or trade stocks. He says the household investments are in a trust his in-laws set up before marriage, managed independently by a third-party trustee. He says neither he nor his wife directs the trades. He also points out that he supports the TRUST in Congress Act, which would bar members of Congress, their spouses, and their dependent children from trading individual stocks while in office. Here's the obvious question. If spouses and dependent children belong inside the ban, why are voters supposed to pretend spousal and child trusts are irrelevant right now? That's the contradiction. Not that there's proven insider trading. There is no public evidence proving that. The contradiction is that Khanna wants credit for supporting a ban that recognizes the household as part of the ethical problem, while asking voters to treat his own household as some separate universe. That IS the Democratic hypocrisy. Give Him the Credit He Earned Khanna does have a real anti-PAC record. He launched the NO PAC Caucus in 2017, aimed at limiting PAC influence and prohibiting PAC contributions to members of Congress. He also joined Summer Lee, Pramila Jayapal, Rashida Tlaib, and others on the Abolish Super PACs Act in 2025. This is not an argument that Ro Khanna has never done anything right. This is an argument that Democrats should stop confusing a well-timed rebrand with conviction. Matt's Take: Ro Khanna is somebody I have been following for many years. I have seen him many times on and other podcasts. In the beginning, Ro Khanna was honestly refreshing. He seemed authentic. He seemed like a congressman who had his positions pretty much locked down and was advocating for them. Then something changed. He changed. Politics changed. And he saw opportunity. Then he started pandering. The problem is that his pandering feels inauthentic and hypocritical compared to the life he lives and the politician he used to be. If he is a rich tech bro, be a rich tech bro. But you cant be Mamdani in politics with a rich tech bro life. It doesn't make sense. Ro is hanging out with union workers like he is friends with them, Like he even knows any laboror, that isn't cleaning his house, in real life. It is like when Mark Zuckerburg was BBQ'ing and told everyone he loves Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce. Like he was trying to convince us he was a real person that does real things. Like Mark, you are not fooling anyone. Go sit down and just be rich. | | ---|---|--- It is obvious that he is trying to build some sort of robust coalition that is outside of who he actually is. He is trying to speak the language, and he is convincing a lot of people. But to be perfectly honest... I do not buy it. The hypocrisy around his accounts and trading is what really bothers me too. It's okay if you have money. It's okay if you are doing well for yourself and your family. I have no problem with that. But actively trading while in Congress, whether it is in a trust or not, and doing very, very well for yourself while in office does not sit right with me. Especially when he is preaching there should be not stock trading in congress and is the author of the TRUST in Congress Act. To me, it sounds like virtue signaling. It gets people to stop looking at him while he stock trades, makes a lot of money, panders, and makes inroads for some sort of power grab with inauthentic positioning. Another Thiel Trojan Horse? Laura's Take Ro Khanna is an opportunist. He takes whichever position is selling that year and leaves his money exactly where it is. In 2016 he ran as Silicon Valley's candidate, funded by the tech industry that had backed him since his first run at Mike Honda in 2014. In 2026 he is co-writing a billionaire wealth tax with Bernie Sanders. He is still the third-heaviest stock trader in Congress, $55.7 million across nearly 4,000 trades, while carrying his own bill to ban members of Congress from trading stocks. I believe Khanna does things like this because he knows the value of performative politics and understands it will never pass. Again, he is buying good will without doing any actual work. Ro Khanna is no better than Donald Trump in this category. Trump continues to use public office to grow his own fortune, and Khanna, no doubt, relies on insider-trading of some sort to do the same. He has no working-class record, so he buys proximity to one. He endorsed Brian Poindexter, an ironworker in Ohio, Zohran Mamdani, a democratic socialist in New York, and Senate candidates in Maine, Michigan, Iowa, and North Carolina, none of them his home state. Not one of those endorsements changed a line in his own financial disclosures. They changed his photographs and his personal brand marketing. Khanna represents Silicon Valley, by many measures the wealthiest congressional district in the country. The ironworkers, steel towns, and warehouse workers he now stands beside are not his constituents, but they now serve as his backdrop. The real Ro Khanna is "wet-fingered" (see the show Veep and its definition of the politics of Qataris) and if it became trendy to jump off bridges tomorrow, he'd be the first one to go. Who is Ro Khanna? Nobody as any actual idea. Stay Angry. Sources: Join otherANGRY DEMOCRATS by support Matt's work. Subscribe and Share! | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Matt Diemer Berea, Ohio ? ?

name: AOC
subject: I’ve got your back.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
What the MAGA movement wants is for all of us to give up and say, “America has gone to hell in a handbasket, and we’re done.”
**No.**
If you are a hard-working, innocent person: **I have got your back**.
If you are just trying to make it in this world: **I’ve got your back**.
If you’re not trying to hurt anybody: **I got your back**.
It’s so important that we affirmatively assert that because, now more than ever, there are a lot of people who don’t know who they are safe with.
But when we speak up, we signal to others that there are people in this world who have not given up.
There are times when we are _not_ in positions of greater power, and sometimes what we are able to do is very limited. But even in times when our hands are tied, **one of the most enormously powerful things we can do is keep the light on**.
Don’t let these people’s bullsh*t get you down. What is so important for us to understand is that as long as we don’t give up, **it’s not over**.
We’re going to keep standing with trans people.
We’re going to keep standing with the LGBTQ+ community.
We’re going to keep standing for the working class.
We’re going to keep fighting for a better minimum wage.
We’re going to keep fighting to guarantee healthcare.
They’re relying on us giving up. **Hell no**.
We will not be afraid – because that’s what they want.
[Help us continue the fight with a grassroots contribution today.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260710.Vuit5V&refcode=em20260710-11899-P_FND_EGR_GRM&t=3&akid=11899%2E2526796%2ESby01i)

In solidarity,
Alexandria

name: Voto Latino
subject: Markwayne Mullin must step down immediately
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
#
One death is enough, Peter.
On July 7th, ICE agents murdered another member of our community, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo.
Lorenzo, a dedicated father of three and construction worker, was fatally shot on his way to work in what appears to be a horrific case of mistaken identity over the vehicle he was driving.
_**Peter, how many more members of our community are we going to allow to die at the hands of our government?** _The Department of Homeland Security must be held accountable — we refuse to let our community continue to suffer while Secretary Markwayne Mullin and DHS get away with it.
[**Add your name to our petition to demand the immediate resignation of DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin.**](https://act.votolatino.org/sign/mullin-resign/?source=em20260710-362&t=1&akid=362%2E1366028%2ET4oiXi)
Lorenzo wasn’t the first person shot under Mullin’s watch, but sadly, he was the first to die. **Under Mullin's group of ICE agents, they’ve shot at least 6 people on our streets.**
But it doesn't stop there — since Mullin took over as DHS Secretary, 6 people have died while in ICE detention. The system has become so broken and deadly that in this year alone, at least 21 people have died while in ICE custody.
We refuse to let this unchecked aggression become our normal. We need an independent investigation, and we need the person at the top to step down — but it’ll only happen if there’s enough public pressure.
**[Peter, please add your name to our official petition right now to demand DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin step down immediately. One death is enough.](https://act.votolatino.org/sign/mullin-resign/?source=em20260710-362&t=2&akid=362%2E1366028%2ET4oiXi)**
**[Add Your Name ››](https://act.votolatino.org/sign/mullin-resign/?source=em20260710-362&t=3&akid=362%2E1366028%2ET4oiXi)**
Thank you,
Voto Latino

name: David Hogg
subject: This is what Chuck Schumer doesn’t understand
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
Our fundraising has slowed down this summer, and we need you with us to keep building this movement.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260710-1&t=1&akid=3709%2E587540%2EjYu-yG)
Peter, I’m going to tell you about something big Chuck Schumer and the establishment just don’t understand. But first:
**Our fundraising has really slowed down this summer. This is exactly the kind of moment that proves whether our people-powered movement has the strength we say it does.**
With 21 wins and 42 endorsements under our belt and even more on the way, we need to make sure our resources match our momentum. Because while we have had some great wins recently, we still have many critical primary and general election races to compete in between now and November. **[So I’m asking, will you make a $5 contribution now to power our work?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260710_1_politicaldivide.EQM4wd&refcode=em20260710-3709&amount=5&t=2&akid=3709%2E587540%2EjYu-yG)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260710_1_politicaldivide.EQM4wd&amount=5&refcode=em20260710-3709&t=21&akid=3709%2E587540%2EjYu-yG)**
Now here’s what I wanted to tell you.
**People are tired of asleep-at-the-wheel Dems. As tired as they are of Republicans, that hasn’t made them energized to vote for Democrats.**
Working people have more in common with each other than with the people holding all the power in Washington. The divide in our politics is increasingly less left vs. right. _It’s up vs. down._ Working people vs. the billionaires and the ultra-rich donor class running the show.
Voters are seeing through the noise and saying loudly that politicians are bought and sold. That leadership isn’t moving on any of the issues that actually matter to them. You already know what I’m going to say — _they’re right._
**That’s exactly the problem Leaders We Deserve exists to solve.**
We’re backing young Democratic candidates who voters will want to vote for because they see themselves in them. Candidates who understand what it’s like to afford rent, pay off student loans, struggle to find a job, or send their kid to preschool right now because that is their lived experience. Leaders with new ideas and a real plan to fix the issues voters care most about, instead of the same tired electeds who answer to corporate interests not working people and whose only vision for the future is “better than what Trump is offering.”
That is the future I am asking you to step up and support today.
**[We need to keep pushing our Party in the right direction and electing the next generation of fearless leaders. Pitch in $5 or whatever you can today to help us get there.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260710_1_politicaldivide.EQM4wd&refcode=em20260710-3709&amount=5&t=22&akid=3709%2E587540%2EjYu-yG)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260710_1_politicaldivide.EQM4wd&amount=5&refcode=em20260710-3709&t=23&akid=3709%2E587540%2EjYu-yG)**
Thank you,
David Hogg

name: Wes Moore
subject: We can’t let this happen
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1607%2E1086043%2Er-3lrN)
Peter, my opponent has it backwards. He wants to make it easier for criminals to carry guns in public but harder to keep guns off our streets.
**That is not a future I'm willing to accept as governor of Maryland.**
_In three years, we've seen historic reductions in violent crime. Homicides are at their lowest level in decades. Baltimore is on track to have its lowest number of murders since 1970._
Dan Cox would reverse all of it. Less safety. Less accountability. More guns in the wrong hands.
And it just got worse. The Supreme Court struck down campaign spending rules for national parties, and Republicans are ready to pour in money to roll back the progress we've made — from bringing jobs to our state to making our communities safer.
**[We can’t let that happen. We need to make sure we’re able to fight back. Can you chip in today to help us protect what we’ve built and keep fighting for every Marylander?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260710-2.BTlxY9&refcode=em-20260710-2&t=2&akid=1607%2E1086043%2Er-3lrN)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260710-2.BTlxY9&amount=5&refcode=em-20260710-2&t=21&akid=1607%2E1086043%2Er-3lrN)**
**_We cannot run this race with anything less than our all, Peter._**
Maryland is _not_ a safe blue seat. We could actually lose – and if we do, Dan Cox will turn back the tide on all the progress we’ve made so far, on public safety and every other priority. **[That’s why I’m counting on your support today.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260710-2.BTlxY9&refcode=em-20260710-2&t=22&akid=1607%2E1086043%2Er-3lrN)**
I’m grateful you’re part of this team.
Elevate,
Wes

| | Dear Faithful Friend,
This year, as we mark 250 years in this great experiment in liberty, I keep asking myself the same question: _**Are we keeping the faith?** _
Let me explain what I mean.
At the very heart of it, _we were born a nation of Christian pilgrims and dissenters. _
The Pilgrims. The Puritans. The Quakers. The Huguenots. The German Pietists. Wave after wave of men and women who crossed an ocean because they refused to let any earthly power stand between them and their biblical faith in the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob – the God revealed in Jesus Christ.
_That is the seed America grew from_ , and every time we’ve forgotten this, we’ve gone astray.
The very first freedom in the Bill of Rights – the one the framers put first, not fifth or tenth, but first – is **the freedom to worship God without interference from government**. That wasn’t random. It was the whole point.
And when people knock our founding fathers as relics of a bygone era who “wouldn’t understand the world today,” I ask you to think about our brothers and sisters in Christ today, _right now_ , in places like Nigeria, Iran, Pakistan, North Korea and many other places.
**There are an estimated 388 million Christian men, women and children being persecuted, oppressed and ruthlessly murdered simply for loving Jesus.**
Here in America, _it’s almost impossible to know what that’s like_ , but we do have the freedom, the platform and the resources to support them, and fight back in a wide range of ways. **The question is, will we?**
I can’t help but feel that this year, on the 250th birthday of the world’s most indispensable Christian nation, that we have a duty to rededicate ourselves to God and to the defense of His people around the world. **And today, I’m asking you to partner with me and an incredible organization in that endeavor.**
**There is no organization in this country more committed to that fight than Save the Persecuted Christians, where I’m proud to serve as a board member.** ** ** Whether it’s the growing awareness of the active genocide against Nigeria’s Christians (and recent U.S. action to help stop it), or the recent and very real victories against the rise of sharia and Islamism here in America, it is due in very large part to the relentless advocacy and education campaigns of Save the Persecuted Christians and the coalition of 200+ organizations they help to guide.
[ **As we commemorate America’s 250th birthday, I humbly but urgently ask that you help to supercharge their efforts with a generous, tax-deductible contribution.** ](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=0874e21840fb475ab669abd2ec408d9f&_e=pJ8BD36UDMRVbltQ-ASe-tuxC3ote1t-5PA89LSBUbdUrhwO_3uPyWsN8jauSHbSholiqKE8OCkc0tqhJ71r-Gzmbg1Q3GUxxX9dtzEci_aqoKQwqNqoDfsS2rnJlBRxXSwxnQMw-nXt5CiGYrbdsZLznH-lMISRBALuo0xMXHc-pbvX1MOoA9aPbcjZfYy2_T74ns8ZUuCbHDGItuVwoH8oN2onKonQd9U1JLAXyczIAlGsL21K-gFAp5y7cuXgalx92mtYMDsH0aEdIAxCCPQutzpE3k_3UudCSO5u6H20Wm6KaSlH5HfxFx4nHSyuS0L_kOnYPgceP6e4tBedA7wSkcI2IlfRxyZ9yK--21dS60OPEIxq5EcTokfn041lPSuoEHtcC9kNZyZj1zFUk4ptJTx7a8FyKZp2jFZjQ_TKtj_g1aUJvsyYf1zWU1ilQhJX-tH2JYm8P9Z1p0y6IoJWWDHXBMPB9uEk-o9kQUzOAv38W0473pwoythuk2_uxCIXPQTEmxaThow221_8z4bERbEXKABfQW7cUYTmF6mMGwdHnHPOd4sTN_AK_yPYI8rxdJY47bURqW8SCs0NmoS5phB51XI2jV8WcgMx6Fy1d5I979ftEzw_tWYQwFHTdZg2TUue3iIqr3Djur6CWYr7cwn8of-uF8OV8wPDwiblPfCUxIItfgTswcowiobj9Ho6P7dTkYU-40GI6mdfEgRwO5BxbxxnyctTjFZLt8WPwHl09myCsY_Hj-Kep8mZ)

As you contemplate your potential commitment, I ask you to think about this.
**While Christians in America today are the freest Christians in the history of the world, 388 million of our brothers and sisters, in other parts of the world, are being hunted for practicing the same faith that built this country.**
Every generation that ever mattered to the kingdom of God understood that faith without action is sentiment – and sentiment has never freed a single soul.
**Now it's our turn.**
Two hundred and fifty years ago, the founders pledged their lives, their fortunes, and their sacred honor. _They paid the price._ They handed us the inheritance. The only real question this year is what we do with it.
On July 3, 1776 – one day after the Continental Congress had voted to declare independence – John Adams sat down in Philadelphia and wrote to his wife Abigail.
He told her this new American holiday " _ought to be commemorated, as the Day of Deliverance, by solemn Acts of Devotion to God Almighty. It ought to be solemnized with Pomp and Parade, with Shews, Games, Sports, Guns, Bells, Bonfires and Illuminations, from one End of this Continent to the other, from this Time forward forever more._ "
Notice the order. _First solemn devotion to God._ Then the fireworks.
250 years later, we’ve kept the fireworks. But the question is, have we maintained the devotion?
I believe we still can. **This anniversary is bigger than a birthday party. It is a reckoning** – with our history, with our blessings, and with our obligations to the brothers and sisters around the world who are paying the highest possible price for the very faith we still get to practice openly.
They are praying for a Church that does not always remember their names.
On this 250th birthday – of all years – we have the chance to tell them they are not forgotten.
[ **That is what your gift does. That is what Save the Persecuted Christians does. And that is why, I am asking you to give as generously as you possibly can.** ](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=0874e21840fb475ab669abd2ec408d9f&_e=pJ8BD36UDMRVbltQ-ASe-tuxC3ote1t-5PA89LSBUbdUrhwO_3uPyWsN8jauSHbSholiqKE8OCkc0tqhJ71r-Gzmbg1Q3GUxxX9dtzEci_aqoKQwqNqoDfsS2rnJlBRxXSwxnQMw-nXt5CiGYrbdsZLznH-lMISRBALuo0xMXHc-pbvX1MOoA9aPbcjZfYy2_T74ns8ZUuCbHDGItuVwoH8oN2onKonQd9U1JLAXyczIAlGsL21K-gFAp5y7cuXgalx92mtYMDsH0aEdIAxCCBUvoFMDlt1hiIVbTQN_ngrwRW6ZChtPc0nLCaSPk6i6eB0e3tVPIgjVz_JO3tJxhNROwcKmc8CzfuCUqsemTxE95KEjN-1Rc9g77QhN0O3rqtL0g7Lq8tlMYkJ5D-PDjSQZGvGzdPhwHBWK_nUjS-IO9JGY56OlNVyWOqI7v2Sn_bhcmNXgZOXExwURsXDnE7eBu7bHNkd5lbSjlb1WK5SI818oPYlkQIuMA7BqpfGzT5TiBRNqaVp5MH5ZyGdd0k46e17GoMhn3ZWQqhXCVR8uzdRHkf6Pen_8xbVm1_ZkXR3tF9LEN5hr4fsuKv_ps3aeCRA2TDB5OZqu77vPG3I9VKKxNIrvAFg0Lyxnn77sdP5rdSCEUhUZ0phoi73ctt10JayXHJf-gzrzGoGST5GV8WnA29TalJe2pjDdpUbwy4-AzZXqJZlTmfETs36B36HJPZnCuTxrC1aCrjkKByp1InjvQOeywPeUz9x0k7Cn)

Whether it’s the growing awareness of the active genocide against Nigeria’s Christians (and recent U.S. action to help stop it), or the recent and very real victories against the rise of sharia and Islamism here in America, it is due in very large part to the relentless advocacy and education campaigns of Save the Persecuted Christians and the coalition of 200+ organizations they help to guide. | "MAKE A GIFT TODAY" As you contemplate your potential commitment, I ask you to think about this. While Christians in America today are the freest Christians in the history of the world, 388 million of our brothers and sisters, in other parts of the world, are being hunted for practicing the same faith that built this country. Every generation that ever mattered to the kingdom of God understood that faith without action is sentiment – and sentiment has never freed a single soul. Now it's our turn. Two hundred and fifty years ago, the founders pledged their lives, their fortunes, and their sacred honor. They paid the price. They handed us the inheritance. The only real question this year is what we do with it. On July 3, 1776 – one day after the Continental Congress had voted to declare independence – John Adams sat down in Philadelphia and wrote to his wife Abigail. He told her this new American holiday " ought to be commemorated, as the Day of Deliverance, by solemn Acts of Devotion to God Almighty. It ought to be solemnized with Pomp and Parade, with Shews, Games, Sports, Guns, Bells, Bonfires and Illuminations, from one End of this Continent to the other, from this Time forward forever more. " Notice the order. First solemn devotion to God. Then the fireworks. 250 years later, we’ve kept the fireworks. But the question is, have we maintained the devotion? I believe we still can. This anniversary is bigger than a birthday party. It is a reckoning – with our history, with our blessings, and with our obligations to the brothers and sisters around the world who are paying the highest possible price for the very faith we still get to practice openly. They are praying for a Church that does not always remember their names. On this 250th birthday – of all years – we have the chance to tell them they are not forgotten. Thank you for your time, your patriotism, and your commitment. For God and country, Eric Metaxas Member, Board of Directors Save the Persecuted Christians | | | "SAVE CHRISTIANS" | | | | | | | | Save the Persecuted Christians PO Box 543 Monument, CO 80132 USA

name: LeftNet
subject: How many more innocent people are going to be killed on American soil by the United States government?
body:
DHS can’t keep getting away with murder.
#
**On July 7th, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was killed by ICE agents in broad daylight in Houston, Texas.**
This shouldn’t have happened, and this should _never_ happen again. Point blank. Period.
Lorenzo’s life in the United States was the true embodiment of the American dream.
He was a hard worker who had been married to his wife for 35 years. He worked tirelessly to provide a future for his three children, who all went on to build successful careers, and he had just achieved his biggest dream of building a home of his own. A house he could finally live in, just like the hundreds he helped build for other families.
He had no criminal record and was close to finishing the long process of regularizing his immigration status. But because of the reckless, unchecked aggression driven by the Trump administration's immigration crackdown, federal agents stole his life.
To make this even more disturbing and twisted, DHS confirmed that Lorenzo wasn't even the intended target of their operation.
Which leaves us with a question._**How many more innocent people are going to be killed on American soil by the United States government? How many more times are we going to let them get away with it?**_
The bloodshed has to stop.
We must collectively stand together right now. We need to organize, mobilize, and vote to elect leaders who will actually bring real oversight and hold DHS accountable for these systemic abuses.
**[Will you stand in solidarity with the family of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo and demand an independent investigation and real accountability for lives stolen by ICE?](https://act.leftnet.org/sign/dhs-accountability/?source=em20260710-1680&t=1&akid=1680%2E2118727%2EeQiHcC)**
**[Add Your Name ››](https://act.leftnet.org/sign/dhs-accountability/?source=em20260710-1680&t=2&akid=1680%2E2118727%2EeQiHcC)**
Thank you,

---

One point, friends.
A new poll just came out here in Michigan, and I'm ahead of Abdul El-Sayed by one point.
One. That means nothing is decided.
This is now a two-way race, so every conversation, every knocked door, every ballot that gets filled out at a kitchen table over the next few weeks truly matters.
And I want to be clear about the stakes here in Michigan because they go way beyond me.
_The Cook Political Report_ - one of the most respected, nonpartisan election forecasters in the country - put it plainly: _" If El-Sayed wins the primary, Democrats have little chance of holding the seat."_
That's the independent judgment of the people whose entire job is calling races straight.
Republicans have reached the same conclusion: It's why the GOP is quietly pushing ads to boost Abdul El-Sayed. They're doing math, too, and their math says they'd rather face him than me in November.
The fact is, Michigan will decide control of the U.S. Senate. It's a must-win for Democrats. Which means this primary isn't just about choosing a nominee. It's about whether this seat stays blue and whether there's a check on Donald Trump's agenda - or one more rubber stamp for it.
This is a critical moment because, right now, somewhere in Michigan, there's a voter opening their ballot and considering their options.
Absentee ballots are out. Election Day is less than a month away. This is the part of the campaign where we hit the gas.
This is a make-or-break stretch, friends. A one-point race, ballots in hand, a month on the clock, and the GOP spending millions to pick their preferred opponent.
I have never been more clear-eyed about what it takes. I came up in Michigan manufacturing - I know what it looks like when the margin for error is zero, and the only answer is to outwork and out-hustle everybody. That's what we're going to do. That's the Michigan way.
Every county. Every door. Every single day until Aug. 4.
If you're in Michigan and you're voting absentee, make your plan and get that ballot in. If you can talk to one friend, one neighbor, one cousin about this race, do it while people are still deciding.
And if you're in a position to chip in to help us reach voters in this final stretch, I'd be truly grateful. Now is the time when your support helps a ton. But no pressure - I'm not asking for thousands. This is a grassroots campaign, and I'm asking for $20 or $30 or whatever you can afford to help us knock more doors and make more calls while the ballots are out. Anything helps in a race this close.
[Chip in](https://substack.com/redirect/931ae8d6-a2cb-4342-8ca0-30551b82f25d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
One point up. One month out. Lots of work to do.
Let's go.
With grit,
Haley

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

This is a critical moment because, right now, somewhere in Michigan, there's a voter opening their ballot and considering their options. Absentee ballots are out. Election Day is less than a month away. This is the part of the campaign where we hit the gas. This is a make-or-break stretch, friends. A one-point race, ballots in hand, a month on the clock, and the GOP spending millions to pick their preferred opponent. I have never been more clear-eyed about what it takes. I came up in Michigan manufacturing - I know what it looks like when the margin for error is zero, and the only answer is to outwork and out-hustle everybody. That's what we're going to do. That's the Michigan way. Every county. Every door. Every single day until Aug. 4. If you're in Michigan and you're voting absentee, make your plan and get that ballot in. If you can talk to one friend, one neighbor, one cousin about this race, do it while people are still deciding. And if you're in a position to chip in to help us reach voters in this final stretch, I'd be truly grateful. Now is the time when your support helps a ton. But no pressure - I'm not asking for thousands. This is a grassroots campaign, and I'm asking for $20 or $30 or whatever you can afford to help us knock more doors and make more calls while the ballots are out. Anything helps in a race this close. One point up. One month out. Lots of work to do. Let's go. With grit, Haley A personal note from Haley 👋 I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love. But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican. I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win. If you're with me, will you chip in today? | | | (C) 2026 Haley for MI 33717 Woodward Ave #539, Birmingham, MI 48009 ? ?

From Michigan to New York, U.S. Sen. Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) recently took Democrats to task for their embrace of far-left, socialist candidates.

On Thursday, Britt said on Fox News Channel's "Hannity" that the Democratic Party has lost its way and is now "beholden" to radicals who don't have America's best interests at heart.

"I think what we are seeing is beyond alarming, and I think the Democratic Party has been taken over by the far left, by the Democratic Socialists of America, and what we find is the common thread between all of them is that they actually hate America," Britt said. "When you look at the policies they are putting forth — their policies that ultimately take away our freedoms — they create dependency on government."

Britt, who grew up in Enterprise, took questions from attendees during the event, giving residents a direct line to their senator on issues affecting the region.

$203M directed to Alabama rural healthcare

At the top of Britt’s agenda was rural healthcare. She announced $203 million has been delivered to the state of Alabama to address the sustainability of its rural healthcare system.

Tommy Tuberville (R-Auburn) and Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) co-bylined an op-ed that appeared Tuesday on AL(dot)com, which praised President Donald Trump and his administration's efforts to move construction forward on the long-awaited new I-10 Mobile River Bridge and Bayway. In the op-ed, Alabama's two U.S. Senators touted the administration's move to eliminate "the final obstacles standing in the way of this transformational project," which includes reported improvements to toll authority, "flexibility" on federal grants and the removal of "unnecessary bureaucratic requirements and commitments from the project scope." | | DOTHAN, Ala. (WTVY) - U.S. Sen. Katie Britt headlined the Dothan Area Chamber of Commerce’s “Eggs and Issues DC” forum Thursday morning, addressing a crowd of business leaders, community members and local residents on rural healthcare funding and children’s online safety. Britt, who grew up in Enterprise, took questions from attendees during the event, giving residents a direct line to their senator on issues affecting the region. $203M directed to Alabama rural healthcare At the top of Britt’s agenda was rural healthcare. She announced $203 million has been delivered to the state of Alabama to address the sustainability of its rural healthcare system. | | | | | | | I didn’t run for Senate to sit on the sidelines. I’m a mom, a conservative, and proud to stand for every corner of Alabama—our cities, small towns, and rural communities alike. body:
And join us for these Fran-tastic events
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260710-3017)
Peter,
One of the best parts of this campaign has been watching supporters across Wisconsin turn big ideas into real community.
This week is packed with volunteer-led events that bring people together in all kinds of ways — over food, games, conversations, and organizing. Whether you're looking to meet fellow supporters, bring the kids, or simply learn more about our vision for Wisconsin, there's something for everyone.
## **THIS WEEKEND**
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16426?t=1&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
[**Milwaukee Policy Lotería** ](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16426?t=2&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
Saturday, July 11 | 1–3:30pm | Sugar Maple, Bay View
Fran's policy platform, reimagined as a Lotería deck by local artists. Policy Director Tim Faust calls the cards and breaks down what each policy means for you, and winners take home prize baskets stocked with gift cards and swag from Sweet Smoke BBQ, Lion's Tooth, and other local favorites. Stick around for the card auction at the end, with all proceeds going toward making these policies real. $15 entry (donate ahead or pay by QR code at the door).
[RSVP ](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16426?t=3&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
****
[**Farm to Fork with Fran & Dan** ](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16427?t=4&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
Sunday, July 12 | 12:30–4:30pm | Wegmueller Farm, Monroe
Chef Francesca Hong and fourth-generation farmer (and fellow chef) Dan Wegmueller are teaming up for an afternoon in Green County: a walking farm tour at 1pm, a street taco cooking demo at 2pm, and food and conversation at 3pm — digging into agriculture, our food system, and Fran's plan for Wisconsin. Family friendly. RSVPs appreciated but not required.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16428?t=5&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
[**Let's Cookout for Fran** ](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16428?t=6&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
Sunday, July 12 | 1–4pm | Shorewood
Burgers, brats, hot dogs, and grilled veggies, plus an art build! Sign-making supplies provided; bring your own craft project if you've got one going.
[RSVP](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16428?t=7&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
**COMING UP**
[****](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16429?t=8&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
[**Postcards & Potluck** ](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16429?t=9&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
Saturday, July 18 | 4–9pm | Cottage Grove
A backyard potluck at a fellow Fran fan's home. Bring a dish (the more random the spread, the better), a chair, a friend, a yard game, and the address of someone who needs a postcard from you. Lemonade provided, kids welcome.
[RSVP](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16429?t=10&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
[****](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16430?t=11&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
[**Parents for Fran Playdate** ](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16430?t=12&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
Saturday, July 18 & Sunday, August 9 | 10am–12:30pm | Madison (address shared when you RSVP)
Political events don't always work with little ones in tow — this one does. Parents connect and talk about the issues facing Wisconsin families while the kids hit the playground, sandbox, bouncy house, and water table. Light refreshments provided. Whether you're all in or just starting to pay attention, you're welcome here.
[RSVP](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16430?t=13&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
[****](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16431?t=14&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
[**Friends of Fran: No Experience Necessary — Milwaukee** ](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16431?t=15&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
Tuesday, July 21, 6–8pm & Sunday, August 2, 3–5pm | Milwaukee (address shared when you RSVP)
New to the campaign? This is your open door. Meet other supporters in your community, find a volunteer role that fits your time and talents, and leave with simple, confident talking points for the conversations that matter most. One quick step first: complete the volunteer form at franhong.com/volunteer before you attend.
[RSVP](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16431?t=16&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
[_Plus: our volunteers are knocking doors every single week._](https://act.francescahong.com/go/11140?t=17&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
[_Find a canvass near you →_](https://act.francescahong.com/go/11140?t=18&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
* * *
**Can't make it to any of these?**
You can still pull up a seat at the (virtual) table. Every one of these events is organized by volunteers and powered by grassroots supporters.
**[Your donation of $10, $25, or whatever feels right keeps this movement growing through August 11.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260710.rxvF3Y&refcode=em20260710-3017&t=19&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260710.rxvF3Y&amount=5&refcode=em20260710-3017&t=22&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)**
See you out there,
Team Hong
**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_fh_footer?refcode=em20260710-3017&t=23&refcode2=3017_105371_DQinuL&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)**
---
Email us: [info@francescahong.com](mailto:info@francescahong.com)
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is one of the most powerful tools that grassroots campaigns like ours have to reach everyday people across Wisconsin and beyond, so thank you for reading to the end.
The more people who engage with our emails, the more likely we’ll go straight to your inbox. For a free and easy way to help our campaign, please [click this link to our website](https://francescahong.com/) after you finish reading our emails.
* [Receive Fewer Emails](https://act.francescahong.com/signup/receive-fewer-emails/)
* [Update My Personal Information](https://act.francescahong.com/signup/did-your-information-change/?t=24&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)
* [Unsubscribe](https://act.francescahong.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=25&akid=3017%2E105371%2EDQinuL)

body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20260710-2469-foote&t=1001&akid=2469%2E342411%2ESCPVBL ]Squad Victory Fund

Peter,

We’re less than a month out from Rashida’s primary election on August 4th,
and right now, she’s got two challengers running against her.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20260710-movement.yZ2Xsv&refcode=em20260710-2469&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=2469%2E342411%2ESCPVBL ][IMG]

Rashida is a fighter and one of the boldest voices in Congress who’s
standing up as outside forces work to control our government. She’s called
out billionaires and corporations, and taken on Trump’s authoritarian
power grabs even when it was easier to stay quiet.

She didn’t go to Congress to keep the status quo. She went to fight for
progressive change and for what her community and our country deserves.
And she’s backed it up.

Since taking office, her district has seen more than $70 million in direct
investments because she fought for it — money to expand housing and
shelter access, grow local jobs, modernize water infrastructure, build up
community spaces, repair roads, and keep public services running.

These are promises Rashida made and delivered for her community. But she's
not done yet, and winning this primary is how she keeps fighting.

We cannot let either challenger take Rashida's seat, and that's exactly
what the Squad Victory Fund exists to stop. We run on people-powered

Chip in $5 today. It truly makes a difference, Friend.

body:
You need to know about this... | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/andyfornevada/friday-weekly-5857752?e=6736d7bc47)

---
| | Dear Peter,

In case you missed it, Brittany Sheehan of Nevada News & Views [provided yet more evidence](https://us.list-manage.com/5A9B74_HP38?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73) today for why Nevada needs an Office of Inspector General:

_"Attorney General Aaron Ford has spent months bragging about a record year fighting Medicaid fraud. His office claims it recovered more than $40.9 million in restitution and won 36 criminal convictions in 2025._

_"Now Ford has a problem. When a state lawmaker asked Nevada's own health agency to confirm those numbers, the agency couldn't do it. Not even close."_

Sheehan adds that:

_"When directly asked to confirm Ford's $40.9 million figure, the [Nevada Health Authority] stated it 'cannot confirm whether the state has received recoveries related to these 36 cases or the referenced $40.9 million.'"_

You’ll likely recall that during the 2025 Nevada Legislature Session, I proposed a bill to create an Office of Inspector General that would be empowered to audit any entity that receives state money.

This is exactly the kind of troublesome situation an Inspector General would be able to look into, to ensure that you, as a taxpayer, get the transparency and accountability you deserve when it comes to state finances.

Republicans, including Governor Joe Lombardo, supported my bill.

Democrats killed it.

But I’m determined to bring it back if re-elected as Nevada Controller this year.

If you can, I hope you’ll [pitch in a contribution](https://us.list-manage.com/ErAMGduKKRs?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73) to help my effort. You can do so by clicking [here](https://us.list-manage.com/Bpuw33VWvg1?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73).

By the way, hats off to Nevada Assemblyman Blayne Osborne for his work on this issue. It was his letter to the Nevada Health Authority that brought this concern to light.

Thanks as always for your support, and I’ll be back in touch with you soon!

For Nevada’s future,

clean_body: You need to know about this... | | | | | | | Dear Peter, In case you missed it, Brittany Sheehan of Nevada News & Views today for why Nevada needs an Office of Inspector General: "Attorney General Aaron Ford has spent months bragging about a record year fighting Medicaid fraud. His office claims it recovered more than $40.9 million in restitution and won 36 criminal convictions in 2025. "Now Ford has a problem. When a state lawmaker asked Nevada's own health agency to confirm those numbers, the agency couldn't do it. Not even close." Sheehan adds that: "When directly asked to confirm Ford's $40.9 million figure, the [Nevada Health Authority] stated it 'cannot confirm whether the state has received recoveries related to these 36 cases or the referenced $40.9 million.'" You’ll likely recall that during the 2025 Nevada Legislature Session, I proposed a bill to create an Office of Inspector General that would be empowered to audit any entity that receives state money. This is exactly the kind of troublesome situation an Inspector General would be able to look into, to ensure that you, as a taxpayer, get the transparency and accountability you deserve when it comes to state finances. Republicans, including Governor Joe Lombardo, supported my bill. Democrats killed it. But I’m determined to bring it back if re-elected as Nevada Controller this year. If you can, I hope you’ll to help my effort. You can do so by clicking . By the way, hats off to Nevada Assemblyman Blayne Osborne for his work on this issue. It was his letter to the Nevada Health Authority that brought this concern to light. Thanks as always for your support, and I’ll be back in touch with you soon!
